_label: MEASURED -- real Verilator RTL cosimulation of the full top-level datapath, not estimated
scope: 1,110,000 transactions per variant (200,000 per single-mode stage x4 + 100,000 mixed-mode + 3 x 70,000 adversarial-pattern stages: dense long Q4_0-encode burst, dense alternating Q4_0-encode/Q8_0-encode, dense random-mode), randomized valid/ready backpressure in the non-dense stages, 4 reset-safety stages (mid-stream flush, reset while Q4_0 encode divider busy -- both checked 0 fails before per-mode stages begin), id/mode/data checked every retirement, 200,000-cycle no-progress deadlock watchdog active throughout (never triggered). Identical workload to Phase B3's own comparison (results/b3-full-datapath.json) -- baseline/B1/B2 numbers below are reproduced from that same run (not re-simulated, since nothing about those 3 variants changed), B4 is new this phase.

b4.note: Same B2-style full-serialization scheduling (q4enc_inflight blocks all issuance while one Q4_0 encode is in flight) -- NO Phase B3 reorder buffer. The entire improvement here comes from the radix-4 divider itself completing roughly twice as fast as B2's radix-2 divider (see results/b4-differential.json: B4 general-path latency ~15 cycles vs. B2's ~28), which proportionally shrinks BOTH Q4_0 encode's own latency AND the serialization window that collaterally delays the three untouched chains -- exactly the direct-speedup hypothesis this phase set out to test, not a scheduling change.

deadlock_watchdog: 200,000-cycle no-progress bound, active on every stage of every variant, never triggered
